This is the API Settings panel. Let\'s expand it to see the configuration options inside.
This is where you enter your Gemini API key. Get a free key from Google AI Studio (aistudio.google.com). The Gemini key powers the AI Dungeon Master chat and Rules Advisor.
This is where you enter your HuggingFace API key for AI-generated scene illustrations during Dungeon Master sessions. Sign up at huggingface.co to get a free token.
Tap this card to open Character Creation. Build fully detailed D&D characters with name, race, class, ability scores, combat stats, background, and starting inventory.
Tap this card to open the Scenario Creator. Design custom adventure settings with time periods, locations, NPCs, plot hooks, and AI GM rules for the Dungeon Master.
Tap this card to open the Dice Roller. Roll dice using standard notation like \"2d6\" or \"d20\" with animated results and a full roll history log.
Tap this card to open the Map viewer. Import map images, place location markers and character tokens, draw colored annotations, and save your map data.
This is the AI Dungeon Master \u2014 the centerpiece of the app. Start AI-powered adventures using your characters, scenarios, and maps. Supports solo play, AI parties, and hot-seat multiplayer!
This is the Ambient Radio. Tap it to browse background music stations and set the mood for your adventure. Music keeps playing as you use other screens.
Use the Dark Mode toggle to switch themes. Tap the gear icon to access Settings, where you can enable Developer Mode for mid-game HP, stamina, and inventory editing.
Start by entering your character\'s name \u2014 this is the only required field. All other fields have sensible defaults. We\'ve filled in \"Thorin Oakenshield\" for this demo.
Choose your character\'s race from 9 options: Human, Elf, Dwarf, Halfling, Gnome, Half-Elf, Half-Orc, Tiefling, or Dragonborn. Each brings different flavor. We\'ve selected Dwarf.
Choose your character\'s class from 12 options like Fighter, Wizard, Rogue, or Cleric. Your class shapes your combat style and abilities. We\'ve selected Fighter.
Set your character\'s starting level (1\u201320). Most new adventures begin at level 1, but you can start higher for experienced characters. We\'ve set level 5.

These are your six core ability scores: STR, DEX, CON, INT, WIS, and CHA. Modifiers are auto-calculated using (score \u2212 10) / 2. You can also set a max point budget and add custom abilities. We\'ve filled in demo values.

Set your combat stats: Hit Points (health), Armor Class (defense), Stamina (action energy), Speed (movement in feet), and Initiative (turn order bonus). We\'ve filled in demo values for a level 5 Fighter.
Choose a Background (Soldier, Sage, Criminal, etc.) and Alignment (Lawful Good through Chaotic Evil). Add freeform Notes for personality, backstory, or goals. We\'ve selected Soldier and Lawful Good.
Set your Carry Capacity (max inventory slots) and add Starting Items with names, descriptions, and durability values. These items become your character\'s inventory in Dungeon Master sessions.
Tap Save to store your character locally. If you save with the same name, it overwrites the existing entry \u2014 great for updating characters between sessions.
Your saved characters appear here. Tap any character to load it back into the form for editing. Tap the trash icon to delete a character (with confirmation).
Enter dice notation here: \"d20\" for one 20-sided die, \"2d6\" for two 6-sided dice, \"3d8\" for three 8-sided dice. Supports 1\u2013100 dice with 2\u20131000 sides each. We\'ve filled in \"2d6.\"
Tap Roll to execute the dice roll. You\'ll see a rapid number animation followed by the final result with a satisfying bounce effect!
Your roll result appears here in a large card showing the dice notation and the final number. The result animates in with a bounce for a fun tabletop feel.
Every roll is logged in the Roll History below, showing the dice notation and result. History persists for the current session so you can track all your rolls.
Enter a name for your scenario. This identifies it when selecting scenarios for AI Dungeon Master sessions. We\'ve filled in \"The Lost Mine.\"
Describe the time period for your adventure (e.g., \"Medieval era, Year 1400\"). This helps the AI set the right historical and cultural tone for the story.
Describe the physical setting \u2014 a forest, city, dungeon, or any location. The more detail you provide, the richer the world the AI builds around your characters. We\'ve added a sample.
List key NPCs the party might encounter: allies, enemies, merchants, quest-givers. Give them names and brief descriptions so the AI can bring them to life in dialogue and events.
Write the opening situation or quest that kicks off the adventure. This is the first thing the AI Dungeon Master reads to begin the story. We\'ve added a sample quest.
Choose how long you want the adventure to last: Short (5\u201310 encounters), Medium (15\u201325), Long (30\u201350), or Epic (50+). This guides the AI\'s pacing.
Set how many NPCs and Locations the AI should weave into the story. Leave these blank to let the AI decide on its own.
Add custom rules for the AI DM, like \"No character deaths\" or \"Extra treasure drops.\" You can also set Stamina Recovery Per Turn (0 = no recovery). These shape the AI\'s behavior.
Tap Save to store your scenario locally. Saved scenarios can be selected when starting a new AI Dungeon Master session to set the adventure\'s world and story.
Your saved scenarios appear here. Tap any scenario to load it for editing. Tap the trash icon to delete a scenario (with confirmation). Save with the same name to update.

string-array.name: guide_bodies
string-array.item: Board games are at their best when you\'re actually playing them \u2014 not buried in rulebooks, rolling physical dice, or spending half the night on setup. This app handles the busywork so you can focus on playing.\n\nFrom the home screen, tap any card to jump into a feature. Build characters, design scenarios, roll dice, annotate maps, stream background music, or run entire adventures with an AI Dungeon Master \u2014 everything is right here. Below is a detailed walkthrough of each feature.

Before using AI-powered features, you need to configure your API keys. Tap the "API Settings" card on the home screen to expand it.

• Gemini API Key — Required for the AI Dungeon Master chat and Rules Advisor. Get a free key from Google AI Studio (aistudio.google.com).
• HuggingFace API Key — Required for generating scene illustrations. Sign up at huggingface.co to obtain a token.

Enter each key in its field and tap "Save." A green "Configured" label confirms it is stored. Tap "Clear" at any time to remove a key.

Create fully detailed D&D characters to use in your adventures.

• Fill in basic info: name, race (9 options from Human to Dragonborn), class (12 options from Barbarian to Wizard), and level (1–20).
• Set your six core ability scores (STR, DEX, CON, INT, WIS, CHA). Modifiers are calculated automatically using the standard formula: (score − 10) / 2.
• Add custom abilities with the "Add Custom Ability" button. Each custom ability has its own name, score, and auto-calculated modifier.
• Optionally set a Max Ability Points budget. A running total tracks your point spend — it turns green when under budget and red when exceeded. You cannot save a character that exceeds the budget.
• Configure combat stats: Hit Points, Armor Class, Stamina (action energy), Speed (movement in feet), and Initiative (turn order bonus). An optional Max Combat Points budget works the same way as ability points.
• Add flavor with background (13 options from Acolyte to Urchin), alignment (9 alignments from Lawful Good to Chaotic Evil), and freeform notes for personality, backstory, or goals.
• Set a Carry Capacity (max inventory slots) and add starting items with names, descriptions, and durability values. These items become your character's inventory in Dungeon Master sessions.
• Tap "Save" to store your character locally. Saving with the same name overwrites the existing entry — great for updating characters between sessions.
• Saved characters appear in the list at the bottom. Tap any character to load it back into the form for editing. Tap the trash icon to delete (with confirmation).

Design custom adventure settings that the AI Dungeon Master can use. Scenarios let you skip the prep work and jump straight into a tailored adventure.

• Give your scenario a name, then describe the time period (e.g., "Medieval era, Year 1400") and setting (e.g., "A cursed coastal city").
• List key characters and NPCs — allies, enemies, merchants, or anyone the party might encounter.
• Write a plot hook: the opening situation or quest that kicks off the adventure.
• Fine-tune the AI GM Settings to control the adventure's scope:
 – Run Length: Short (5–10 encounters), Medium (15–25), Long (30–50), or Epic (50+).
 – NPC Count and Location Count guide how many the AI weaves into the story.
 – Custom Rules let you set directives for the AI DM, like "No character deaths" or "Extra treasure drops."
 – Stamina Recovery Per Turn controls how much stamina characters regain each turn (0 = no recovery).
 – Rulebook: By default, the AI DM uses a built-in D&D 5e SRD summary for game mechanics. Tap "Upload .txt" to upload a custom rulebook file (e.g., homebrew rules or a different game system). The AI will follow your custom rules instead. Tap "Clear" to revert to the default. Custom rulebooks are saved with the scenario.
• Tap "Save" to store your scenario. Saved scenarios appear at the bottom. Tap to load, trash icon to delete. Save with the same name to update.

A full-featured RPG dice roller with history tracking.

• Enter standard dice notation: "d20" for one twenty-sided die, "2d6" for two six-sided dice, "3d8+5" for three eight-sided dice plus a modifier of 5.
• Tap "Roll!" to see your result with an animated bounce effect.
• Supports 1–100 dice at a time, with 2–1000 sides per die.
• Your roll history is displayed below, showing every roll from the current session with dice notation, individual results, and totals.
• Input validation catches mistakes before you roll — you'll see a clear error message if the notation is invalid.

An interactive map viewer and annotation tool for your game world.

• Tap the "+" button to import any image from your device as a map.
• Use the zoom controls to zoom in and out, and drag to pan across the map.
• Place location markers: Tap the pin icon, then tap anywhere on the map to drop a labeled marker (e.g., "Dragon's Lair"). Tap a marker to delete it.
• Place character tokens: Tap the character icon to enter character placement mode, then tap the map to place a named character token.
• Draw annotations: Tap the brush icon to enter drawing mode. Choose from 8 colors using the palette button. Draw paths, borders, or highlights directly on the map.
• Erase drawings: Tap the eraser icon, then tap any stroke to remove it. Long-press the eraser to clear all drawings at once.
• Clear everything: Use the "Clear All" option to remove all points, characters, and drawings from the map in one step.
• Your map, points, and drawings are automatically saved when you leave the screen. Unsaved changes will prompt you before exiting.

The centerpiece of the app — a fully AI-powered Dungeon Master for interactive RPG sessions.

SETUP:
• Select one of your saved characters. The AI receives your character's full stats, inventory, and backstory for context-aware storytelling.
• Optionally select a saved scenario to set the adventure's world, NPCs, rules, and plot. Skip this to let the DM create the setting on the fly.
• Recruit other saved characters as party members, or choose "Solo (No Party)" to adventure alone.
• Mark which party members are human-controlled for hot-seat multiplayer. Unchecked members are AI-controlled. Tap "All AI" to make everyone AI.

GAME MODES:
• Cooperative — All players work together against the adventure's challenges.
• PvP (Competitive) — Players compete against each other. Choose Open visibility (everyone sees all actions) or Hidden (actions are secret until resolved).
• PvP Teams — In PvP mode, assign players to teams or use "Randomize" for random team assignments. Free-for-all is also available.

TURN ORDER:
• Solo / AI Party: The DM narrates, you act, then AI party members respond automatically (green chat bubbles).
• Hot-Seat Multiplayer: After the DM narrates, each human player takes a turn. A "Pass the Phone" prompt appears between players. Human messages appear in teal bubbles.

COMBAT & STATUS:
• HP tracks your health. Reaching 0 HP causes unconsciousness; further damage causes death. Dead characters cannot act and skip their turns.
• Stamina tracks action energy. Reaching 0 Stamina causes exhaustion — exhausted characters can speak but cannot take physical actions. Stamina can recover each turn if configured in the scenario.
• The AI automatically adjusts HP and Stamina based on combat, healing, and story events.
• Tap "Open Status" to view HP, Stamina, and inventory for your character and all party members.

INVENTORY:
• Items have names, descriptions, and durability values. Use or Drop items from your inventory.
• When the AI awards loot, items are added automatically. If your inventory is full, loot goes to an Unclaimed Loot pool where any party member can pick it up.
• Trade items between party members using the Trade option.

OTHER FEATURES:
• NPC and enemy dialogue appears in purple chat bubbles with character names.
• Tap "Illustrate" to generate an AI illustration of the current scene (requires HuggingFace API key). Tap the image to view fullscreen.
• Use "New Run" to start a fresh adventure. Tap the character info card to switch between past runs.
• Map Integration: Toggle map access to let the DM see and modify your map — creating locations, placing tokens, and moving markers as the story unfolds.
• Rulebook: The AI DM always has access to a detailed rules reference. By default it uses a built-in D&D 5e SRD summary. If your scenario includes a custom uploaded rulebook, the AI uses that instead — great for homebrew systems or house rules.
• Rules Advisor: Tap the info button to ask rules questions without affecting your adventure. The advisor has access to the same rulebook as the DM (default SRD or your custom upload) and knows your character's stats for tailored answers.
• Developer Mode: When enabled in Settings, you can manually edit HP, Stamina, and add inventory items mid-game for testing or custom scenarios.

Set the mood for your adventures with background music that plays across all screens.

• Tap the radio bar at the bottom of the home screen to open the station picker.
• Browse available stations and tap any station to start streaming.
• Music continues playing as you navigate between Character Creation, Dice Roller, Map, and Dungeon Master sessions.
• Tap the stop button on the radio bar to stop playback at any time.
• The app handles audio focus automatically — music ducks when other apps play audio and resumes when they stop.

• Create your characters and scenarios before starting a Dungeon Master session — the more detail you provide, the richer the adventure.
• Create multiple characters with distinct stats, classes, and backstory notes to use as party members with different play styles.
• For hot-seat multiplayer, create a character for each human player beforehand. During setup, select them as party members and mark them as human.
• For PvP, try "Hidden" visibility mode with teams for the most strategic experience. Use "Randomize" for quick team assignment.
• Set starting items and carry capacity on your characters before a DM session so you begin with gear ready to go.
• Import a map image before your DM session so you can enable AI Map access for dynamic, story-driven map updates.
• Upload a custom rulebook in the Scenario Creator to play with homebrew rules, a different game system, or house rules. The AI DM and Rules Advisor both follow whatever rulebook is active.
• Use the Rules Advisor during adventures to look up spells, ability checks, combat rules, or class features without affecting the main story.
• Enable Developer Mode in Settings to manually adjust HP, Stamina, and inventory mid-game — useful for testing or custom house rules.
• Start the Ambient Radio before a session to set the atmosphere with background music.
• Toggle Dark Mode from the home screen for comfortable play in any lighting.
• The Dice Roller, Character Creation, Scenario Creator, and Map work fully offline — only the AI Dungeon Master and Ambient Radio require an internet connection.
• All your data (characters, scenarios, map annotations, chat history, and adventure runs) is saved locally on your device.
